name: live_scalar_subquery_with_no_match_is_null
description: A scalar subquery that matches no row evaluates to NULL, so its column is nullable even though the selected column is NOT NULL in the schema
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE users (id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, email TEXT, created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now())
CREATE TABLE orders (id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY, user_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id), total NUMERIC(10, 2) NOT NULL, created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now())
query_sql:
-- @name GetUsersWithTheirOnlyOrderTotal
-- @returns :many
SELECT u.id, (SELECT o.total FROM orders o WHERE o.user_id = u.id) AS only_order_total FROM users u ORDER BY u.id

columns.name: only_order_total
columns.note: orders.total is NOT NULL, but a scalar subquery matching no row yields NULL

sqlc_comparison.sqlc_behavior: sqlc takes the subquery column's schema nullability, so a NOT NULL column stays non-nullable however few rows the subquery matches
sqlc_comparison.scythe_improvement: scythe marks a scalar subquery nullable, and the second seeded user has no order at all so the engine returns the NULL

default: INSERT INTO users (id, name, email) VALUES (1, 'Ada Lovelace', 'ada@example.com')
INSERT INTO users (id, name, email) VALUES (2, 'Grace Hopper', 'grace@example.com')
INSERT INTO orders (id, user_id, total) VALUES (1, 1, 42.50)
